properties.areaDesc: Central Siskiyou County
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 13 at 4:12PM PST until November 15 at 1:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 55 mph expected
Saturday night into Sunday. The current high wind threat has ended.

* WHERE...Most of the Shasta Valley in central Siskiyou County. This
includes portions of Interstate 5 as well as the communities of
Weed, Gazelle, Grenada and Montague.

* WHEN...From noon Saturday to 1 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highways running west to east will be exposed
to tough driving conditions given the strong southerly wind speeds.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

Secure large or inflatable holiday decorations. Winds this strong
will be capable of damaging these items.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 3:59PM PST until November 13 at 5:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Portions of Placer, Sacramento, Amador, El Dorado and
Nevada County in California...

* WHEN...Until 500 PM PST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 358 PM PST, local law enforcement reported flooding in the
advisory area. Rainfall is causing urban and small stream
flooding. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Auburn, Placerville, Jackson, Cameron Park, El Dorado Hills,
Lake Of The Pines, Ione, Rancho Murieta, Colfax, Shingle
Springs, Rescue, Coloma, Lotus, Latrobe, Smithflat, Garden
Valley, Pilot Hill, Greenwood and Forest Home.
- Highway 50 and Interstate 80
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 3:53PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15
to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large
breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50
ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over
seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 6 PM PST this
evening. For the High Surf Warning, until 4 AM PST Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is
specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves
will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent
infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 3:03PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 40 feet.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 13 at 12:15PM PST until November 15 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to
7 feet with sets 8 to 10 feet along west-facing beaches. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected,
particularly along west-facing beaches where surf will be
highest.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to
10 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to
4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Adjusted high tides will be near 6.2-6.5
feet around midday on Saturday, which will combine with high
surf to produce minor coastal flooding. Highest surf is expected
to occur late Saturday into early Sunday. Surf begins to wane
Sunday afternoon but will remain elevated into Monday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 13 at 12:05PM PST until November 17 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to
8 feet today, increasing to 8 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights
are expected to decrease to 5 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday.
Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will
we highest for west-northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry,
especially around the time of high tide, including over beach
parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to
significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely
but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning.
Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly
swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with
highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and
potentially again Monday. Minor to moderate coastal flooding
impacts are possible, especially when largest surf overlaps
with peak high tides. Some of these impacts may be moderate to
significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normally dry
beaches and walkways.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 13 at 1:32AM PST until November 14 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
* CHANGES...Earlier start time to account for the arrival of gusty
winds late this morning.

* WHAT...Heavy wet snow. Snow accumulations of 1 to 2 feet above 7000
feet, up to 6 inches between 6000 and 7000 feet, and little to no
accumulations below 6000 feet. Wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph over
ridges and gusts of 55 to 70 mph for areas along Highway 395.

* WHERE...Mono County.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 10 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Friday evening commute. Strong winds and Sierra
cement snow could cause damage to trees and power lines.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A period of strong, gusty winds is expected
late this morning into the afternoon, preceding the arrival of
heavy snow. A burst of heavy snow is likely with this system this
evening into early Saturday morning with snow levels falling to as
low as 6000 feet.
properties.instruction:

vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.
